reviews.review:
I started with EDF 4.1 for context.  I picked up EDF 5 for a little bit more of that.  Hopefully with some nice quality of life improvements. And in some ways there are there, but EDF is still definitely just as rough-around-the-corners still.

The four classes feel a little more balanced that 4.1.  The Ranger does actually feel like the basic class instead of EDF 4.1 Wing Diver.  The Ranger has good weapons, health and sprint with increased aura for pick ups.  

The Wing Diver feels the most nerfed from EDF 4.1.  Initial energy makes it very easy to overwhelm the power used for flight and weapons.  Additionally, Wing Divers really drain their energy meter pretty fast with their weapons and/or have a lot more charge weapons.  The also seem to have lost their bird hop just touching the ground and jump around.  If this was your favorite class in EDF 4.1, I don't know if you will like this game.

Air Raider is a combination of buffs and nerfs.  The basic weapons as well as the radioed in weapons (mortars, cannons, bombers, etc.) feel much more powerful. And the vehicles still feel powerful.  However, as some one that plays the Air Raider just to be a mech pilot, there is a wait to get the credits to finally get the drop.  And many of the early missions, its far too little too late.  Which very much disappoints me personally.

Fencer seems better and slightly easier to use, but still a class I find a little too frustrating to play much. So no comment.

Many of the enemies from EDF 4.1 one are here. However, in the early game the biggest addition in humanoid aliens that have a long range attack and regenerate.  Which I can't say I particularly like.  And they show up pretty early in the game changing the flow from EDF 4.1.  But more the most part it still works like EDF 4.1

Farming is both more difficult to accomplish, but also feels less needed than EDF 4.1  Although, there are still tons of weapons I've tried once and never again.  And this is possibly worst than EDF 4.1 in me not using a wide range of weapons.

EDF 5 is still EDF, I can't say I like it more than EDF 4.1.  In fact, as someone that just really wants to be a mech pilot in the game, I know I don't the way things work.  However, there are probably more ups than downs compared to EDF 4.1.  But nowhere close to enough that if you didn't like EDF 4.1 that EDF 5 is going to change things.  There's still a lot of jank and it takes some time to get okay weapons and understand to deal with the rough controls.  But I still like it enough to give it a thumbs up.
